A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Event-Driven Video Generation and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, human preferences, VBench scores, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds compositional, temporal, simultaneous-event, localization, and baseline comparisons in Appendix A.14.

M1.justification: The event head, event-grounded losses, hysteretic gate, scheduling, and sampling procedure remain unchanged. The training and sampling algorithms move from the main text to Appendix A.8; the new overview figure documents the existing method.

E1.justification: v3 adds a 40-prompt compositional/temporal subset and a 30-prompt simultaneous-event subset drawn from T2V-CompBench and NeuS-V (Appendix A.14). These extend evaluation beyond the retained 150-prompt EVD-Bench to compositional and concurrent-event requirements. Printing the existing EVD-Bench prompt list does not itself add coverage.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates Wan and Hunyuan on EVD-Bench and includes them in the compositional comparison (Table 8). The original quantitative and qualitative comparator sets are retained. GEST, StreamV2V, and other newly discussed related works are not reported as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.14 adds separate 40-prompt and 30-prompt evaluation designs, compositional scores, temporal-order pass rates, event-pair success, interaction-region activity measurements, and additional VBench subdimensions. Existing EVD-Bench generation settings and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged; the new protocols are described only briefly.

E4.justification: v3 adds pseudo-target/activity/gate localization diagnostics (Figure 5), quantitative background-versus-interaction activity, simultaneous-gate analysis, and numerical ordering-loss ablation results (Table 8). v1 already discussed ordering-loss effects and contained motion-mask controls and a schedule sweep; those earlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 specifies bootstrap confidence intervals and Fleiss' kappa but provides no numerical estimates. v3 Table 8 supplies intervals for three human-preference scores and criterion-specific kappa values. The bootstrap procedure, rater counts, and fixed-seed sampling practice are unchanged; additional generation runs are not established.

E6.justification: The original tables retain their numerical results. v3 Table 8 adds substantial results, including compositional scores of 64.8 for EVD versus 58.7/56.9/51.2 for Wan/Hunyuan/DiT-30B, and Wan/Hunyuan VBench Dynamics scores of 91.6/90.8. Its schedule summary reports 94.1/94.8/94.5, whereas the retained sweep reports 94.4/94.8/94.9 at the same listed cutoffs; no setting difference explains this discrepancy.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Flow Matching formulation, losses, event-gating equations, and scheduling derivations remain equivalent across the main text and appendices. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical definition of the added empirical metrics appears.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that a lightweight DiT-compatible event pathway, event-grounded training, and gated sampling improve interaction dynamics while preserving appearance. v3 uses more cautious wording, but the central contribution and claimed scope remain the same.

C2.justification: v3 interprets simultaneous-event results as evidence that token-wise gating permits multiple active regions while global DiT attention couples their effects (Appendix A.14). It also adds a qualification about public endpoints changing behind unchanged model labels (A.16). The existing failure regimes and non-claims are largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 includes all 150 EVD-Bench prompts in Appendix A.12, making evaluation inputs available within the PDF; v1 mentions their release elsewhere but does not contain the list. v3 also identifies NVIDIA GH200 hardware and the NSF/NCSA allocation and adds a project-page address. Training budgets, hyperparameters, and algorithms were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section explicitly positions EVD against GEST and GEST-Engine event representations, and against StreamDiffusion, StreamV2V, and ObjectAlign. T2V-CompBench and NeuS-V also enter the evaluation context. This substantially expands positioning beyond v1's discussion of video backbones and motion steering.

P1.justification: Extensive rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, motivation, contributions, results, conclusion, and appendix explanations. A dedicated Related Work section and reorganized appendix, including relocated algorithms, change the narrative structure. Authorship, affiliation, and acknowledgements are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 adds the method overview and localization figures, a multipage prompt table, and a stress-test summary table. It merges the two headline comparison tables into side-by-side panels, moves the efficiency table into the main text, and relocates the algorithms to the appendix. Existing qualitative frames are retained, with revised captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The complete prompt list, clearer research positioning, localization diagnostics, and numerical uncertainty estimates improve transparency and assessability. The added tests broaden the evidence, but their subset selection and scoring procedures remain underspecified, and Table 8 introduces unexplained schedule-score disagreements with Table 4. These limitations constrain the overall gain despite substantial additions and presentation changes.
